title: Tracking Your Cycles with Inito: Understanding Your Fertility Results
summary: Learn all about tracking your cycles with Inito, including how to interpret your fertility chart, track and confirm ovulation, & decode your hormone trends.
body_markdown:
## What does Ovulation Confirmed Mean in my Cycle?


**Short answer:** Ovulation Confirmed means Inito has detected a steady and consistent PdG rise after your LH surge, indicating that ovulation has likely occurred. Receiving an Ovulation Confirmed result is an important milestone because it means your hormone pattern is consistent with ovulation having taken place. Unlike LH, which predicts ovulation, PdG provides confirmation that your body has responded to the LH surge and released the egg.


### When did I ovulate?


Since ovulation typically occurs 24-36 hours after your true LH surge, **Inito marks your Ovulation day as Peak Fertility day + 1.** This means,


-


If the latest Peak Fertility was detected on **CD16** ,


-


Your ovulation day = **CD17**


### What can I expect next?


**Entering the luteal phase:** After ovulation, your body shifts into the luteal phase. During this phase, progesterone remains elevated to help support the uterine lining in case pregnancy occurs.


### Do I need to keep testing?


Further testing isn’t required after ovulation has been confirmed. However, some people like to continue tracking to monitor their overall cycle patterns.


**The two-week wait:** The stretch between ovulation and your next period (or a positive pregnancy test) is often called the **two-week wait** . It can feel long and emotionally charged, so be gentle with yourself. This is the perfect time to focus on rest, nourishment, and self-care.


**Know more:**[Your Complete Guide to Surviving the Two-Week Wait](https://blog.inito.com/the-two-week-wait/)
